title: review findings are written by a verb, every validator warning family carries a code the lint can see, and a fresh worktree's evidence is counted
desiredOutcome: A sign-off's findings and their resolutions are recorded through a verb under the lock with a journal row, and the outcome's tally is derived from them; the stable-code lint reaches every warning _check_phase_gate emits; check-example-ledgers judges pointers and ledgers over the same set, so a phase's second task gate in a fresh worktree is not red on the first gate's pointer.

findings.issue: resolve-finding marks a finding as fixed by a task that has not landed. _fix_commit checks only that a commit exists and that it agrees with task.commit. A task in `pending` status, with no commit recorded, is accepted whenever --commit is passed. I reproduced this on a scratch copy of docs/audit: `finding P86 ...` then `resolve-finding P86-R1 --fix-task P86.1 --commit <scratch HEAD>` exited 0 alt

A defect in an uncommitted manifest is no longer caught until it is committed, and the OK line does not say so. I tested this on a clone of HEAD. I edited docs/audit/phases/P78.json in the working tree: P78.1's cached status changed from passed to failed against its ledger run, and its commit changed to deadbeef…. The base tool exited 1 with two FINDINGs, a cache disagreement and an unresolvable c

Findings written by concurrent `finding` calls from one session are lost, and each call still reports success. When the session already holds the lock, _acquire_lock says 'already yours -- nothing was taken', so calls from one session are not serialized. I ran six `finding P81` calls in parallel with the same CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID on a scratch plan. All six exited 0 and each printed 'P81-R1 recor

The tally's 'N with a fix commit' clause counts only entries carrying fixTask and commit, which only resolve-finding writes. The existing plan records 242 object findings, and none of them carries either field, because their fixes were recorded in the resolution text. So the first verb write to any older phase produces a derived clause that contradicts the phase's own prose. I ran `correct P74 --r

_review_target refuses only a cancelled phase. `finding` therefore appends to a phase that is already signed off and merged, and rewrites that phase's review.outcome with no note. I confirmed this on P85, which is passed and done. A tally the verdict was never given against is written into a closed record, and the output does not say the phase already has a verdict.

The group sign-off path (`signoff P1,P2 --branch`) now derives the tally, and the task claims 'both signoff paths'. No case asserts it: the rv cases (rv7) drive only the single-phase signoff. Reverting line 7348 to `args.review_outcome.strip()` would leave test_audit_task green.

A finding's fixTask and commit are copies taken when resolve-finding runs, and the tally derives from those copies. `reopen` clears task.commit (audit-task.py:4153 puts None) but does not touch review.findings. After the fix task is reopened, the finding still says 'fixed in X (sha)' and the tally still counts it. I found this by reading the code; I did not run it.

The journal row records review.outcome from and to in full, but _journal_row truncates long values ('… [truncated]'). The tally sits at the end of the outcome, so for any real outcome the two values print identically and the row does not show what changed. I saw this in the P85 review.finding row on the scratch copy.

tasks.title: a verb records a sign-off finding and its resolution, and the outcome's tally is derived from the findings
tasks.description: F516 (quality-gates-internal PLAN.md). Add a verb that appends a finding in the schema's shape (id, severity low|med|high, file, issue, resolution) under the index lock, revalidating or rolling back, with a review.finding journal row; a way to set a finding's resolution to its fix task and commit when the fix lands; and derive the severity tally in review.outcome from review.findings when the verb writes it, so no one types it. A text-only correction of review.outcome or summary goes through a verb with its own journal row and never re-decides the verdict. phase-signoff.md step 1 names the verb. Red-first: a malformed finding (missing severity, severity outside the vocabulary) is refused before any write; allow: a well-formed one is appended and journaled; a correction leaves the verdict and its row untouched.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a finding with a severity outside low|med|high can only be written by hand, and nothing refuses it

outcome.technical: finding, resolve-finding and correct verbs under the index lock with journal rows; outcome_with_tally on every review.outcome write.
outcome.descriptive: Sign-off findings and their fixes are recorded by a command instead of a hand edit, and the outcome's tally can no longer disagree with the list.

tasks.title: the stable-code lint reaches every warning the phase-gate checks emit
tasks.description: F517 (quality-gates-internal PLAN.md). _check_phase_gate mutates the validator's warnings parameter, a shape fc2's walk never follows, so the whole family can ship uncoded. Give _check_phase_gate (and its helpers) the return shape the walk already follows - it returns its findings and the caller extends - rather than adding a new seed rule. Red-first: strip the code from one _check_coupling warning and fc2 goes red; allow: every coded site stays green and the validator's output is byte-identical before and after.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__output.py: repro that FAILS on current code - stripping the code from a _check_coupling warning leaves fc2 green

outcome.technical: _check_phase_gate returns its findings for the caller to extend; the walk reads a feeder's early literal return.
outcome.descriptive: Every warning the phase-gate checks emit now carries a stable code, and the lint would catch one that does not.

tasks.title: check-example-ledgers judges pointers and ledgers over the same set
tasks.description: F519 (quality-gates-internal PLAN.md). The tool reads pointers from the working-tree manifests but counts only git-tracked ledgers, so a phase's second task gate in a fresh worktree goes red on the first gate's pointer into the still-untracked evidence file. Judge both halves over the same set - read pointers from manifests at HEAD (the committed claim this tool exists to check). Red-first: a fixture repo whose tracked manifest at HEAD has no pointer to the untracked ledger while the working-tree manifest does passes; allow: a manifest at HEAD pointing at a run no ledger holds still fails.

add: tools/check-example-ledgers.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a manifest pointer into an untracked ledger file in a fresh worktree fails el2

outcome.technical: check-example-ledgers reads pointers and ledger rows at HEAD through one git cat-file batch.
outcome.descriptive: A task gate in a fresh worktree no longer fails because an earlier gate's evidence file is not committed yet.

tasks.title: the review verbs refuse an unlanded fix, write safely in parallel, say what their tally counts, and stay true after a reopen
tasks.description: Phase review of P84 (review-P84.json), findings 1, 3-8. (1) resolve-finding refuses a fix task that is not done, --commit or not; a case. (3) parallel calls from one session lost findings because the lock lets its own session back in (_locks.py:889): find why re-entry is keyed on the session; make it re-entrant only for a child process that carries the holder's token (so a verb's own subprocess still gets in) and serialise every other caller, including another process of the same session; add `finding --findings-file` that records several findings in one write; phase-signoff.md step 1 names the batch form and says the per-finding form is one at a time; a real parallel case (several processes, one session id) where every finding lands. (4) the tally's clause says exactly what it counts ("k with a recorded fix commit"), never implying the rest are unfixed. (5) `finding` refuses a phase that has landed (mergedAt set) with the reason; on a signed-off, unlanded phase it records the finding and says so in the row. (6) a case for the group sign-off tally path. (7) reopen clears the fix task's commit from every finding that recorded it, so the tally stops counting it; a case. (8) the journal row's from/to of a long outcome is shortened from the middle so the tally at its end stays visible.

tasks.title: check-example-ledgers judges the working tree's pointers against every ledger the working tree holds
tasks.description: Phase review of P84 (review-P84.json), finding 2. P84.3 moved the whole pointer half and the commit-reference check to HEAD, so a defect in an uncommitted manifest (a wrong cached status, a fake commit) now passes before the commit and goes red only after it - the gate stops seeing what it exists to catch. Judge the working tree instead, over one consistent set: the working tree's manifests' pointers against every ledger file the working tree holds, tracked or untracked, and the working tree's commit references - which is what fixes the original fault (a pointer into a still-untracked ledger) without hiding pre-commit defects. Red-first: the reviewer's shape (a wrong cached status and a fake commit in a working-tree manifest) fails; the original P84.3 case (a working-tree pointer into an untracked ledger) still passes; the tool passes on this repository. The CHANGELOG line for this lands with P84.4's commit (the orchestrator adds it).

add: tools/check-example-ledgers.py: repro that FAILS on current code - an uncommitted manifest edit giving a task a wrong cached status and a fake commit passes

outcome.technical: check-example-ledgers judges the working tree's tracked manifests against every ledger file it holds, tracked or not.
outcome.descriptive: A defect in an uncommitted plan file is caught before its commit again, and a pointer into an evidence file not yet committed still resolves.
